candidate.answerReason: The only interior stationary point is x=1. Comparing its value with both endpoint values gives a maximum of 3 at x=3.

methods.label: Derivative and endpoint test
methods.explanation: \(f'(x)=2x-2\), with a stationary point at \(x=1\). Since \(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=-1\), and \(f(3)=3\), the maximum value is \(3\).
methods.levelReason: The retained main method uses polynomial differentiation and the closed-interval candidate test taught in this elective.

methods.label: Completing the square
methods.explanation:
Completing the square makes the size of \(x-1\) control the function value:
\[
f(x)=(x-1)^2-1.
\]
For \(0\le x\le3\), we have \(-1\le x-1\le2\), so \((x-1)^2\le4\). Thus \(f(x)\le3\). Equality occurs at \(x=3\), where \(f(3)=3\), so the maximum value is \(3\).
methods.levelReason: This alternative uses grade-9 quadratic reasoning and avoids derivatives.
